title: Comparing the locally characterized norm polynomial with the multiplication characteristic polynomial
statement:
Let $A,B$ be commutative rings, $\varphi:A\to B$ unital, $r\ge0$, and $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in A$ generate the unit ideal. Suppose $e_{i,1},\ldots,e_{i,r}$ are bases of the $A_{f_i}$-modules $B_{f_i}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Write $\varphi[T]$ for coefficientwise polynomial extension [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Let $N_T:B[T]\to A[T]$ be any function such that for every $v\in B[T]$ the coefficientwise image of $N_T(v)$ in $A_{f_i}[T]$ is the determinant of multiplication by the image of $v$ on $B_{f_i}[T]$, computed in the constant polynomial basis $C(e_{i,1}),\ldots,C(e_{i,r})$ [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant]. For $b\in B$ let $\chi_b(T)\in A[T]$ be the scalar-extension characteristic polynomial of multiplication by $b$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free-existence], and put $P_b(T)=N_T(T-C(b))$. Then
$$P_b(T)=\chi_b(T)=T^r+\sum_{j<r}a_jT^j\quad(a_j\in A),\qquad (\varphi[T](P_b))(b)=0.$$
In particular $P_b$ is monic of degree $r$ if $A\ne0$. If $r=0$ then $B=0$ and $P_b=1_A$, whose image evaluates to zero in $B$. If $A=0$, unitality forces $B=0$, and the expansion and evaluation remain valid, including for the empty family. No scheme hypothesis or global basis is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free-existence] to multiplication by b and take its specified chosen polynomial χ. For each principal chart, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-tensor] transports the given localized basis to a basis of A[1/fᵢ] ⊗ B. Apply the chosen polynomial’s scalar-extension property over ULift A[1/fᵢ], so its test-ring universe is exactly the prescribed maximum. Base-change compatibility and invariance under tensor cancellation from [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module-properties] descend this identity along the injective ULift map. Naturality on the generators x/1 identifies scalar-extended multiplication with mapExtendScalars of multiplication. Thus the image of χ is the characteristic polynomial of the displayed localized multiplication matrix. The same existence theorem supplies the expansion of χ.

proof.text: Localization of linear maps and toMatrix are additive. They carry multiplication by 1 to the identity matrix. In each matrix entry, expand the polynomial sum for X−C(b) using additivity, the sum formulas for X and C, and preservation of negatives. The result is Xδⱼₖ−C(Mᵢ(b)ⱼₖ). Thus hN at X−C(b) identifies the localized norm polynomial with det(XI−Mᵢ(b)), which is its characteristic polynomial by [def-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module] and the determinant description [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant].

proof.text: For every coefficient k the local identities in steps 1 and 2 give equal images of the coefficients of N(X−C(b)) and χ on all principal charts. Use coefficientwise injectivity of the standard localization cover, the ring case of [lem-weil-pbc-localized-span-eq-zero], to conclude N(X−C(b))=χ. Transfer the expansion from step 1.

proof.text: For the localized multiplication endomorphism μᵢ, prove by induction on n that μᵢⁿ(x/1)=(bⁿx)/1, using naturality of mapExtendScalars. Induction on polynomials, with additive and monomial cases, then identifies localization of (p.map(A→B)).eval(b) with evaluation of the endomorphism polynomial p.map(A→A[1/fᵢ]) at μᵢ, applied to 1/1. Step 2 and basis invariance from [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module-properties] identify this endomorphism polynomial with its characteristic polynomial. Apply [lem-weil-cayley-hamilton-free-module] to get zero. This uses no nontriviality or degree assertion.

proof.text: The preceding calculation shows that z=(N(X−C(b)).map(A→B)).eval(b) maps to zero under every localized-module numerator map. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localized-span-eq-zero] with M=B and the given unit-ideal cover to obtain z=0. The algebra map is never assumed injective.

proof.text: Over a nontrivial A, the lower-degree sum in the expansion has degree strictly below r. The elementary polynomial degree and leading-coefficient formulas [def-weil-polynomial-ring] show that Xʳ plus this sum is monic of natural degree r. If r=0, the sum is empty and the expansion gives N(X−C(b))=1. Its already proved evaluation identity gives 1_B=0_B, hence B is subsingleton. If A is subsingleton, apply the unital algebra map to 0_A=1_A to get 0_B=1_B. All earlier steps hold for zero local rings and an empty cover.

lean.statement: theorem principal_free_norm_polynomial_comparison {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] {r m : ℕ} (f : Fin m → A) (hgen : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤) (e : ∀ i : Fin m, Module.Basis (Fin r) (Localization.Away (f i)) (LocalizedModule.Away (f i) B)) (N : Polynomial B → Polynomial A) (hN : ∀ (q : Polynomial B) (i : Fin m), (N q).map (algebraMap A (Localization.Away (f i))) = Matrix.det (fun j k : Fin r ↦ q.sum fun d c ↦ Polynomial.monomial d (LinearMap.toMatrix (e i) (e i) (IsLocalizedModule.mapExtendScalars (Submonoid.powers (f i)) (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers (f i)) B) (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers (f i)) B) (Localization.Away (f i)) (LinearMap.mul A B c)) j k))) (b : B) : N (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C b) = Classical.choose (charpoly_locallyFree_exists_unique.{u, v, w} f hgen (fun i ↦ ⟨e i, trivial⟩) (LinearMap.mul A B b)) ∧ (∃ a : Fin r → A, N (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C b) = Polynomial.X ^ r + ∑ j : Fin r, Polynomial.C (a j) * Polynomial.X ^ (j : ℕ)) ∧ ((N (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C b)).map (algebraMap A B)).eval b = 0 ∧ (Nontrivial A → (N (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C b)).Monic ∧ (N (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C b)).natDegree = r) ∧ (r = 0 → Subsingleton B ∧ N (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C b) = 1) ∧ (Subsingleton A → Subsingleton B)
